texts.preamble: Mohan Lal vs State on 17 August, 2023 Author: Farjand Ali Bench: Farjand Ali High Court Of Judicature For Rajasthan At Jodhpur S.B. Criminal Revision Petition No. 1119/2003 Mohan Lal S/o Gheesa Lal, by caste Jat, resident of Devaria, P.S. Kapasan, District Chittorgarh. ----Petitioner Versus The state of Rajasthan ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Sanjay Mathur For Respondent(s) : Mr. Abhishek Purohit, Aga Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Farjand Ali Judgment 17/08/2023 1.
texts.facts: Bereft of elaborate details, facts relevant and essential for disposal of the instant criminal revision petition are that the Food (2 of 5) [CRLR-1119/2003] Inspector Labh Shankar Bohra on 16.05.1993 at around 08:00 a.m. reached the shop of the petitioner where he was selling milk which was stored in a container. Upon suspicion, the food inspector took sample of the milk from the accused-petitioner after following the due procedure and sent the same for analysis to public analyst who gave a report Ex. P-12. Finding the same to be adulterated. Thus, after obtaining prosecution sanction, a complaint was submitted against the petitioner in the competent court for the offence under Section 7/16 of the PFA Act. The learned magistrate summoned the accused and after hearing on charge, framed charge against him for the aforesaid offence, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. Hence, this revision petition is preferred by him.
texts.arguments: 3. After arguing the case on merits to some extent, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that he will not assail conviction of the petitioners and confine his arguments to the alternative prayer of reduction of the sentence awarded by the trial court. He submits that there is non-compliance of Section 13(2) of PF Act as one sample was sent for analysis to laboratory at Udaipur and another was sent to the laboratory at Pratapgarh and the report was not supplied to the petitioner which is mandate (3 of 5) [CRLR-1119/2003] of law. He submits that the incident in the present case pertains to the year 1993. The petitioner was 33 years of age at the time of incident and presently, he is aged 63 years. The petitioner has already suffered agony of protracted trial for long 30 years. He was not having any criminal antecedents and it was the first criminal case registered against him. No adverse remark has been passed over his conduct except the impugned judgment. The petitioner has remained in custody for sometime during the trial as well as after passing of judgment of appeal. No fruitful purpose would be served by sending the present petitioner to jail at this stage. With these submissions, learned counsel prays that by taking a lenient view, the sentence awarded to the petitioner may be reduced to the period already undergone by him. 4. Learned public prosecutor has, of course, been able to defend the case on merits but does not refute the fact that the petitioner has remained behind the bars for some time and the case is pending since long.
